messages:
kevin: FYI I just got a support ticket — customer 'AcmeCorp' failed a BYOK rewrap. KMS call returns 400 with 'invalid key version'. They attempted rewrap after we rotated CMK yesterday.

pagerduty-bot: [ALERT] acme-byo-rewrap-failure triggered at 2024-08-01T14:07:02Z (incident #INC-5421)

maria: ugh. any idea if this is RBAC-related? did we change the keystore operator role bindings in the last deploy?

kevin: not in the infra deploys I reviewed. I pulled the audit events from the proxy — see snippet below. looks like the request made it to our KMS-proxy but the upstream cloud KMS rejected it.

olivia: paste the audit lines pls

kevin: ```
2024-08-01T14:06:58Z keystore-proxy request_id=req_9a2 user=acme-operator action=RewrapKey target_key=cmk-0001 version=3 outcome=400 error=invalid_key_version client_ip=34.82.11.9
2024-08-01T14:06:59Z authz check request_id=req_9a2 principal=acme-operator roles=[keystore-operator] allowed=true
2024-08-01T14:07:00Z proxy-upstream request_id=req_9a2 upstream_resp=400 upstream_code=InvalidKeyVersion
```

maria: interesting — authz allowed=true so RBAC doesn't look like the immediate cause. Could be a stale key version or an upstream KMS state problem. Did they try to rewrap to the new CMK or an intermediate?

kevin: they targeted the latest CMK (cmk-0001:v4). Our internal mapping still had v3 marked as latest for that tenant for a minute due to a race during rotation. I think the proxy forwarded v3 but the customer's external entitlement checked v4.

sam: if it's a race, we need a safe fallback: allow rewrap-to-old-version or queue the request until rewrap completes. But compliance: we can't silently fallback to provider-managed key. check policy first.

maria: correct. Compliance note: for customer-managed keys we must not perform any operation that exposes plaintext or uses a provider-managed key without explicit customer consent. Any fallback must be documented and approved by customer and recorded in audit logs.

olivia: can we reconstruct the timeline from our event log and the customer's KMS logs? we need evidence for the postmortem and for customer evidence for SOC2.

kevin: yes. I have proxy logs + request bodies. I've asked Acme for their KMS logs — they already uploaded an export to the ticket. Quick diff shows our proxy sent key_version=3 while their KMS expected 4.

maria: OK action items: 1) contain — add a temporary validation to reject rewrap requests when proxy/latest mismatch detected and return a clear 409 with remediation. 2) evidence collection — gather proxy logs, authz logs, and customer-supplied logs. 3) compliance review — draft incident note explaining why no plaintext was exposed and that no provider key was used. 4) long-term — add atomic rotation handoff in the rotation orchestration to avoid transient dual-latest states.

sam: +1 on 1). I'll open a quick PR to return 409 with message: "rotation-in-progress: please retry after rotation completes" and add a metric to count these events.

kevin: I'll attach logs to the ticket and mark them for legal/compliance. Also adding a script to reconcile key version mapping (one-off repair) so tenants won't be blocked.

olivia: for vuln triage: if an attacker could intentionally trigger a rotation race to cause repeated rewrap failures, could that lead to DoS on customer workloads? we should rate-limit rewrap attempts per-tenant and alert on spikes.

maria: agree. add rate-limits + dashboard alert. Also confirm KMS integration doesn't allow privilege escalation: authz allowed=true in logs above — verify principle binding can't be spoofed.

kevin: note: authN comes from tenant-signed JWT validated by our proxy. replay/forgery checks in place (nonce + iat window). I'll add replay-detector logs to be safe.

sam: for immediate customer support: propose manual reconciliation: run repair script, reattempt rewrap under monitored window, provide customer with signed audit bundle proving no key material left our boundary.

maria: legal wants a templated statement for BYOK incidents that we can send quickly. I'll draft and share. In parallel we should do a tabletop: timeline, who executed repair, who approved any deviation.

olivia: note for KMS integration config: add an explicit lease/state flag that rotation job flips in a single transaction (lease=rotating true -> update mapping -> lease=false) rather than multiple writes. reduces window.

kevin: deploy plan for the fix: hotfix to proxy (409 on mismatch + metric) within next 2 hours, reconcile script, then router/rotation orchestration change in next sprint.

sam: I'll own the proxy hotfix and monitoring; ping me on Slack before deploy so SRE can watch. (react :thumbsup:)

maria: thanks. I'll start the compliance/incident note and loop legal. kevin, attach the audit bundle to the ticket and set the ticket status to 'investigating'.

kevin: done. ticket updated, logs attached. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ACME-872

olivia: adding a follow-up: run a small chaos test in staging to simulate concurrent rotation+rewrap to validate the change before prod.

sam: agreed. schedule it tomorrow.

maria: good work team. we'll reconvene in the incident channel if anything changes.

kevin: closing thread here; will post postmortem draft later today.
